data.title: We're Not Very Worried About Unigold's (CVE:UGD) Cash Burn Rate
data.description:
Even when a business is losing money, it's possible for shareholders to make money if they buy a good business at the right price. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So, the natural question for Unigold (CVE:UGD) shareholders is whether they should be concerned by its rate of cash burn. For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Does Unigold Have A Long Cash Runway?

You can calculate a company's cash runway by dividing the amount of cash it has by the rate at which it is spending that cash. In June 2026, Unigold had CA$10m in cash, and was debt-free. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through CA$2.2m. So it had a cash runway of about 4.6 years from June 2026. There's no doubt that this is a reassuringly long runway. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

View our latest analysis for Unigold

How Is Unigold's Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Unigold didn't record any revenue over the last year, indicating that it's an early stage company still developing its business. Nonetheless, we can still examine its cash burn trajectory as part of our assessment of its cash burn situation. Over the last year its cash burn actually increased by 38%, which suggests that management are increasing investment in future growth, but not too quickly. However, the company's true cash runway will therefore be shorter than suggested above, if spending continues to increase. Unigold makes us a little nervous due to its lack of substantial operating revenue. We prefer most of the stocks on this list of stocks that analysts expect to grow.

Can Unigold Raise More Cash Easily?

Given its cash burn trajectory, Unigold shareholders may wish to consider how easily it could raise more cash, despite its solid cash runway. Companies can raise capital through either debt or equity. Commonly, a business will sell new shares in itself to raise cash and drive growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Unigold has a market capitalisation of CA$61m and burnt through CA$2.2m last year, which is 3.5% of the company's market value. That's a low proportion, so we figure the company would be able to raise more cash to fund growth, with a little dilution, or even to simply borrow some money.

So, Should We Worry About Unigold's Cash Burn?

It may already be apparent to you that we're relatively comfortable with the way Unigold is burning through its cash. In particular, we think its cash runway stands out as evidence that the company is well on top of its spending. While its increasing cash burn wasn't great, the other factors mentioned in this article more than make up for weakness on that measure. Looking at all the measures in this article, together, we're not worried about its rate of cash burn; the company seems well on top of its medium-term spending needs. data.description:

The merger speculation is landing at a tricky time for Tesla investors. The 1‑day share price return declined 7.64% and the 7‑day move is down 11.38%, extending a year‑to‑date share price fall of 21.06%, even though the 3‑year total shareholder return is up 46.88%.

Tesla now trades about 17% below the average analyst target after a sharp pullback, even as rumours of a SpaceX tie up keep expectations high. Is that discount enough to reflect the risks the market is flagging?

Most Popular Narrative: 42% Undervalued

Tesla closed at $345.82 while the most followed Simply Wall St Community narrative pegs fair value at $600.82, implying a large gap that frames how some investors are reading the SpaceX merger talk.

According to Ledora, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the key question is whether Tesla's big product stories can justify that kind of valuation gulf over time.

Tesla remains an interesting stock to watch as investors weigh its long-term growth potential against near-term execution risks. Robotaxi development, Optimus, energy storage and vehicle demand are all important parts of the company''s future, but profitability and cash flow will ultimately determine how sustainable that growth becomes.

See why 38 investors see Tesla as 42% undervalued.

The discount rate used in the narrative is 10.46%, which sets a relatively demanding hurdle for future cash flows yet still supports a fair value well above the current price. That reflects an outlook where the AI, autonomous driving, energy storage and robotics efforts eventually contribute meaningfully on top of the existing $103.57b revenue base and $3.22b in net income, even though profit margins of 3.1% are currently below last year's 5.3%.

At the same time, the narrative sits against some tougher cross-checks. The SWS DCF model suggests Tesla is trading above an estimated future cash flow value of $188.47 and recent statements highlight weaker earnings over the past year and a lower return on equity of 3.6%. That kind of split view is why the merger speculation with SpaceX matters so much for sentiment, because any credible path to higher, more durable profits becomes central to whether a $600.82 fair value feels realistic.

Result: Fair Value of $600.82 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, Tesla faces real pressure if vehicle margins stay thin or if AI and robotics projects take longer than expected to translate into solid earnings.

Another View: Tesla’s Price Versus Sales

The narrative fair value of $600.82 for Tesla leans heavily on long term potential. A simple P/S yardstick paints a very different picture. At 13.2x sales, TSLA trades far above the US Auto industry at 0.4x, peers at 1.1x, and a fair ratio of 3.2x.

That kind of gap means even small disappointments in execution or SpaceX merger expectations could have an outsized impact on the share price, while stronger than expected progress might already be partly reflected in today’s valuation. data.title: What Monolithic Power Systems Doubters Got Wrong
data.description:
Monolithic Power Systems spent much of the year talking about silicon carbide inverters for clean energy and new automotive audio chips, while also rolling out a fresh US$500 million buyback program. For Monolithic Power Systems shareholders, the return over the past year was 31.8%, including dividends. If you had been deciding whether to buy on 20 November 2025, what would you have needed to believe about those products and that capital return plan before any of this played out?

A Narrative on Simply Wall St is one investor's written case for a company, with its growth, margin and multiple assumptions spelled out. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

This theme extends beyond Monolithic Power Systems. See which of 41 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks may still merit a closer look.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On Monolithic Power Systems

The shares cost US$857 at the start of the period, so any view on Monolithic Power Systems needed a clear story about its new projects and cash returns.

The bullish Narrative saw Fair Value at US$940, about 10% above the start price. It leaned on silicon carbide inverters, automotive audio and 24 bit converters gaining traction, as well as a US$500 million buyback and higher dividends supporting earnings per share.

The cautious view put Fair Value at US$750, around 13% below the start price. It focused on delayed ramps in silicon carbide and automotive audio, volatile demand from hyperscalers and AI projects, and slower product launches in enterprise data and industrial segments.

What The Results Changed In The Monolithic Power Systems Story

Record Q3 2026 revenue of US$1.2b and net income of US$271.1m, up from US$737.2m and US$179.8m in Q3 2025, gave the bullish Monolithic Power Systems case support on product traction and capacity plans. The 22.5% net margin, down from 24.4%, along with governance investigations and a securities lawsuit, kept the cautious view alive. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The hinge assumption was that new silicon carbide, automotive and enterprise data lines plus buybacks would add value without eroding quality or controls. For any other stock with a similar story, check whether rising revenue and repurchases are matched by stable margins and clean audit, restatement and legal disclosures.

What Today's Monolithic Power Systems Price Already Implies

With Monolithic Power Systems now at US$1,142, the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St places its Fair Value above that level, based on a detailed earnings and margin path. The storyline leans heavily on AI hungry data centers and a steadily building automotive pipeline.

For that higher Fair Value to be reached, you would need to think Monolithic Power Systems can fill its expanded manufacturing footprint with profitable AI and auto demand while keeping returns intact. The question is whether that capacity plan and supply chain reshuffle keep working at today’s entry price.

"The main factor that has to go right is that Monolithic Power Systems successfully executes its capacity expansion and supply chain diversification while managing costs so that investments in modules, next generation power products and new markets do not erode returns. The current valuation and bullish coverage imply that the share price already reflects strong growth, high margins and effective capital returns such as buybacks and dividends, so the stock is priced for continued successful delivery on this growth plan."
